agreement: All six committees support a disclosure requirement only with conditions.
Disclosure should be concise, neutral, accessible, proportionate, and limited to material uses of generative AI.
Routine administrative, translation, accessibility, grammar, and minor editing assistance should be exempted or handled through simplified disclosure when it does not materially shape the work.
Applicants should report AI roles and impacts, human creative control, consent and acknowledgement, and rights or provenance information reasonably within their knowledge and control.
Disclosure must not operate as an automatic funding penalty, finding of infringement, rights clearance, or substitute for legal review and stakeholder consultation.
Assessment must remain human-led, with guidance, confidentiality protection, good-faith correction, appeal, and proportionate remedies.
Jakarta stakeholder co-design and operational testing are required before any real adoption.
disagreement: Committees place different weight on discipline-specific risks: music prioritizes voice and sound-role attribution; theatre emphasizes evolving ensemble processes; dance emphasizes movement and embodied authorship; film emphasizes digital replicas, production stages, and archives; literature emphasizes translation and expressive text; visual arts emphasizes cultural data, style, fabrication, and curation.
Film proposes staged disclosure at application and final reporting, while other committees mention updates or final notices without converging on one reporting schedule.
Literature and visual arts explicitly raise audience-facing notice design; the other committees focus primarily on funder-facing disclosure.
No shared operational threshold for material use emerged from the evidence pack.
cross_disciplinary_effects: Multidisciplinary work may require one disclosure to cover text, image, sound, movement, performance, identity, curation, and dissemination without duplicative forms.
Voice, likeness, movement, style, cultural heritage, and community-held knowledge can cross committee boundaries and require consent and attribution review.
Translation and accessibility uses can broaden participation across disciplines but could be burdened by an undifferentiated disclosure rule.
Provider-controlled training information is often unavailable to applicants across all disciplines, so attestation should be limited to reasonable knowledge.
missing_evidence: Direct Jakarta stakeholder consultation across all six disciplines.
Existing Jakarta grant application, assessment, contracting, reporting, correction, appeal, and data-handling mechanics.
A locally tested cross-disciplinary definition of material generative-AI use with discipline-specific examples.
Applicant burden, accessibility, digital-literacy, and compliance-cost testing.
Current Indonesian legal analysis specific to AI-assisted authorship, training data, performers' rights, identity imitation, privacy, contracts, and liability.
Evidence about effects on assessment consistency, applicant behaviour, participation, artistic freedom, trust, welfare, and grant outcomes.
A tested framework for confidentiality, correction, enforcement, appeal, and proportional remedies.
missing_stakeholders: Jakarta artists and cultural workers across music, theatre, dance, film, literature, and visual arts.
Disabled, multilingual, community-based, informal, and low-resource applicants.
Performers and people whose voice, likeness, movement, identity, or work may be simulated.
Rights holders, cultural-heritage custodians, source communities, and holders of traditional cultural expressions.
Grant assessors, administrators, legal advisers, archivists, accessibility practitioners, audiences, and technology vendors.
recommendation: For this simulation, require a short, neutral disclosure of material generative-AI use in funded artistic work, but do not implement a real rule until Jakarta stakeholders co-design and test it. Define materiality by substantive effect on expression, authorship, represented identity, consent, rights, curation, fabrication, or public presentation. Exempt or simplify routine administrative and accessibility assistance; request only information reasonably known or controlled by applicants; allow updates and good-faith correction; protect confidential information; keep assessment human-led; and establish guidance, appeal, and proportionate remedies. Treat disclosure as information for accountable assessment, not as a ban, automatic penalty, proof of infringement, or substitute for consultation and legal analysis.
conditions: Complete direct Jakarta stakeholder consultation and co-design.
Define and test material use with general and discipline-specific examples.
Separate minor assistive uses from substantive creative generation.
Limit applicant attestations to reasonably known and controlled information.
Keep grant assessment and decisions human-led.
Protect confidential information and sensitive cultural knowledge.
Create correction, update, appeal, enforcement, and proportional-remedy procedures.
Test accessibility, administrative burden, assessor consistency, and unintended bias before adoption.
Review current Indonesian law separately; do not import foreign legal conclusions.
